title: How to Sell Property in Bangladesh While Living Overseas: Legal Steps, Taxes and Proceeds
metaTitle: Sell Property in Bangladesh from Abroad: Steps & Tax
metaDescription: Step-by-step guide for NRBs selling land or a flat in Bangladesh: documents, buyer checks, Power of Attorney, deed registration, taxes and receiving proceeds.
heroIntro: Selling property from abroad can be as risky as buying it: fake buyers, brokers who demand advance money, delayed payments and tax surprises. A well-planned sale protects both your price and your title. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Selling from Abroad: Quick Facts
points: Prepare clean title documents first: deed, mutation, tax receipts and a deed search.
You can sign the deed in person or through an attorney under a properly attested Power of Attorney.
Take payment by bank transfer or pay order, never full cash, and register the deed only when the main payment is received.
Taxes include capital gains / transfer-related taxes and registration costs; ask your advocate to estimate before fixing a price.
Sending sale proceeds abroad is restricted by foreign exchange rules; plan this with a bank early.

sections.content:
Buyers and banks check the same documents you would check when buying (see our buyer checklist). Fix gaps before listing:

  • Mutation in your name and recent land tax receipts.
  • Certified copies of all earlier deeds.
  • Heirship certificate if the land was inherited, with all heirs ready to sign.
  • A clear map and area measurement.
  • No mortgage, court order or acquisition notice.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

sections.h2: Step 2: Find and Screen the Buyer
sections.content: Use reputable agents but never pay a broker upfront. Check the buyer's identity (NID), source of funds and, if a company, its RJSC registration. Avoid buyers who push for fast cash or ask you to register before payment. A bank-financed buyer is usually safer.

Sign a written agreement for sale with a part payment (earnest money), the balance schedule, a deadline and consequences of default. Describe the plot exactly (dag number, khatian number, mouza, area). Ask your advocate to draft it, and give the buyer a copy signed by both sides.

sections.h2: Step 4: Executing the Deed, Personally or by Attorney
sections.content: If you can travel, signing in person is simplest. If not, give a special Power of Attorney that names this buyer, a minimum price and a time limit (see our Power of Attorney guide). The attorney then signs and registers the deed at the Sub-Registrar office. Never give a general irrevocable PoA to sell, and require the attorney to hand over the money only through your bank account.

On a sale, expect to deal with:

  • Registration fee and stamp duty: usually borne by the buyer by agreement.
  • Source tax / advance tax: collected by the registering office on the transfer.
  • Capital gains tax: may apply depending on the holding period and rules under the Income Tax Act 2023; the rate and exemption change often, so check the current law.
  • Land development tax clearance: up to date at the time of sale.

Ask your advocate or a tax professional for a written breakdown and keep copies of all receipts.

sections.h2: Step 6: Receiving and Sending Money Abroad
sections.content: Take payment into your Bangladeshi bank account. Moving sale proceeds abroad is regulated by the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 and Bangladesh Bank rules; generally, repatriation requires proof of source, tax clearance and permission through an authorised dealer bank. If you plan to move money out, speak to the bank before you sell, so the documents are ready. Alternatively, invest or hold the money in an NRB (foreign currency) account if eligible.

• Registering the deed before receiving the main payment.
  • Accepting cash payments with no receipt.
  • Letting the buyer fill in the deed price below the market price (under-valuation risks tax and legal problems).
  • Forgetting to cancel an old Power of Attorney after the sale.
  • Leaving the mutation to the buyer without a written commitment.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

faqs.question: Can I sell my property in Bangladesh without going there?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a properly attested Power of Attorney and your advocate's help. Signing in person is safer if you can travel.

faqs.question: Is capital gains tax payable on property sale?
faqs.answer: It can be, depending on the current Income Tax Act rules and exemptions. Get tax advice before you fix the price.

faqs.question: Can I send sale money abroad?
faqs.answer: It is possible but regulated. You need proof of source, tax clearance and approval through an authorised bank under Bangladesh Bank rules.

faqs.question: Who pays registration cost, buyer or seller?
faqs.answer: By custom the buyer pays registration fee and stamp duty, but this can be agreed in writing.

faqs.question: What if the buyer does not pay the balance?
faqs.answer: Do not register the deed. You can cancel the agreement per its terms and keep earnest money, or file a suit for breach of contract.
